Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 63, verses 1–2:

On the interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿When the hypocrites come to you, they say, "We testify that you are the Messenger of Allah." And Allah knows that you are His Messenger, and Allah testifies that the hypocrites are liars.﴾ (1)

He, the Exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿When the hypocrites come to you﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿they say﴾ with their tongues, ﴿"We testify that you are the Messenger of Allah. And Allah knows that you are His Messenger"﴾. Whether the hypocrites said that or did not say it: ﴿And Allah testifies that the hypocrites are liars﴾. That is, Allah testifies that the hypocrites are liars in their report about themselves that they testify that you are the Messenger of Allah, because they do not believe that and do not have faith in it; so they are liars in their report of it.

Some of the people of Arabic grammar used to say concerning His words, ﴿And Allah testifies that the hypocrites are liars﴾: it is only that their inner state lied, because they concealed hypocrisy. Just as their faith was not accepted, though they had displayed it, likewise He made them liars, because they concealed other than what they displayed.

* *

On the interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿They have taken their oaths as a shield, and so they have averted [people] from the way of Allah. Indeed, evil is what they have been doing.﴾ (2)

He, the Exalted, says: the hypocrites have taken their oaths as a shield, namely their swearing.

As:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿They have taken their oaths as a shield﴾: that is, their oaths are a shield.

* Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning the word of Allah: ﴿They have taken their oaths as a shield﴾, he said: they conceal themselves behind them, and he said that because they believed and then disbelieved.

* I was told by al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say concerning His words ﴿They have taken their oaths as a shield﴾: their oath by Allah that they are surely of you.

* *

As for His words ﴿a shield (junnah)﴾: a cover behind which they conceal themselves, as one who seeks cover behind his shield in battle and fighting, protecting by it themselves, their offspring and their wealth, and warding off harm from them by it.

The people of interpretation have said what is similar to what we have said.

Those who said that:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿a shield﴾: so that they might protect their blood and their wealth by it.

And His words ﴿so they have averted [people] from the way of Allah﴾: that is, they turned away from the religion of Allah with which He sent His Prophet (ﷺ) and from His law which He prescribed for His creation. ﴿Indeed, evil is what they have been doing﴾: that is, indeed these hypocrites who took their oaths as a shield, evil is what they have been doing in taking their oaths as a shield, because of their lying and hypocrisy, and other of their affairs.

His words, may His remembrance be exalted, mean: Evil is what these hypocrites were doing, those who took their oaths as a shield, because they had testified that God and His Messenger were true, and then they disbelieved through their doubt about that and their denial of it.

* *

As for His words, ﴿so a seal was set upon their hearts﴾:

He says: God placed a seal upon their hearts, sealing them with disbelief against faith. We have already explained the nature of the sealing of the heart, with its proofs and the statements of the scholars, in another place, so that suffices and there is no need to repeat it here.

* *

As for His words, ﴿so they do not understand﴾:

His words, may His remembrance be exalted, mean: they do not understand what is right from what is wrong, or truth from falsehood, because God has sealed their hearts.

Qatadah used to say concerning this:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿That is because they believed, then disbelieved; so a seal was set upon their hearts, and so they do not understand﴾: They professed that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God (ﷺ), but their hearts were denying and refusing that.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 63, verse 4:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And when you see them, their bodies please you; and if they speak, you listen to their speech. They are as if they were propped-up pieces of wood. They think every cry is against them. They are the enemy, so beware of them. May Allah destroy them; how are they deluded?﴾

His Lord, exalted is His remembrance, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): And when you see these hypocrites, O Muhammad, their bodies please you because of the evenness of their form and the beauty of their appearance. ﴿And if they speak, you listen to their speech﴾: that is, He, exalted is His praise, says: if they speak, you hear their speech, which resembles the speech of people. ﴿They are as if they were propped-up pieces of wood﴾: that is, these hypocrites are as if they were propped-up pieces of wood, with no good in them, no understanding, and no knowledge. They are only forms without minds, and shapes without intellects.

* *

And His words: ﴿They think every cry is against them﴾

That is, He, exalted is His praise, says: these hypocrites, out of their wickedness, their evil opinion, and their lack of certainty, think every cry is against them, because they fear that Allah will send down a matter that exposes their concealment and disgraces them, and permits the believers to kill them, take captive their offspring, and seize their wealth. So, out of their fear of that, whenever a revelation came down from Allah to His Messenger, they thought that it had descended to bring about their destruction and ruin. Allah, exalted is His praise, says to His Prophet (ﷺ): They are the enemy, O Muhammad, so beware of them, for when they meet you, their tongues are with you but their hearts are against you, with your enemies; they are a spy for your enemies against you.

* *

And His words: ﴿May Allah destroy them; how are they deluded?﴾

That is: may Allah disgrace them; in what direction are they turned away from the truth?

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, and I heard him say concerning the words of Allah: ﴿And when you see them, their bodies please you﴾ ... the verse, he said: these are the hypocrites.

The readers differed concerning the recitation of His words: ﴿as if they were propped-up pieces of wood﴾. The majority of the readers of Medina and Kufa, except al-A'mash and al-Kisa'i, recited ﴿khushubun﴾ with a damma on the kha and the shin, as if they directed it to a plural of a plural: they pluralized khashaba (a piece of wood) as khishab, then pluralized khishab as khushub, just as thamara (fruit) was pluralized as thimar, then thumur. It may also be that khushub with a damma on the kha and the shin is the plural of khashaba, with the shin sometimes vowelled and sometimes sukun, just as they pluralized akama (hillock) as akam and akam, with the kaf sometimes vowelled and sometimes sukun, and as it is said: al-budun and al-budn, with the dal vowelled and sukun, for the plural of badana (camel for sacrifice). Al-A'mash and al-Kisa'i recited it as ﴿khushbun﴾ with a damma on the kha and sukun on the shin.

The correct view on this is that both are well-known recitations and eloquent dialects, and whichever of them the reader recites is correct. Sukun on the middle letter in the case of the plural of fu'ula to fu'l among nouns is more common in the speech of the Arabs, as in their pluralizing badana as budn, and ajama as ujm.

**The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:** ﴿And when it is said to them, "Come, the Messenger of Allah will ask forgiveness for you," they turn their heads aside, and you see them turning away while they are arrogant.﴾

Allah, may He be remembered and exalted, says: When it is said to these hypocrites, "Come to the Messenger of Allah so that he may ask forgiveness for you," they twist their heads, meaning they shake and wag them, mocking the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his request for forgiveness.

Regarding the doubling of the waw in ﴿لَوَّوْا﴾ (lawwaw), the reciters (qurra', the Qur'an readers) read it as a report about them, that they repeatedly wagged and shook their heads and did so often. The exception is Nafi', who read it with a single waw, ﴿لَوَوْا﴾ (lawaw), to indicate that they did this only once.

The correct view on this matter is the reading of the one who doubled the waw, because the consensus (ijma', the agreement of the authoritative scholars) of the reciters is upon it.

* *

And His saying: ﴿and you see them turning away while they are arrogant﴾

Allah, may He be remembered, says: "And you see them turning away from what they were called to, with their faces, ﴿while they are arrogant﴾," meaning they are arrogant about going to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to ask him to forgive them.

As has been reported, these verses all refer to Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, because he said to his companions: "Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of Allah until they disperse," and he said: ﴿If we return to Medina, the mightier will surely expel the meaner from it﴾. Zayd ibn Arqam heard this and informed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) summoned him and asked him about what he had reported. He swore that he had not said it. It was then said to him: "If only you would come to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and ask him to forgive you." He began twisting his head and shaking it in mockery, meaning that he would not do what they had advised him. So Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed this entire surah concerning him, from beginning to end.

Interpreters (ahl al-ta'wil, those who explain the Qur'an) have said things similar to what we have said, and reports have come to that effect.

Mention of the report that came with this:

• Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Adam narrated to us, saying: Israil narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Zayd ibn Arqam, who said: "I went out with my uncle on a military expedition, and I heard Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul say to his companions: 'Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of Allah until they disperse. If we return to Medina, the mightier will surely expel the meaner.'" He said: "I mentioned that to my uncle, and my uncle mentioned it to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He sent for me, and I told him. He sent for Abd Allah and his companions, and they swore that they had not said it." He said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) considered me a liar and believed them, and I was struck with a grief the like of which had never struck me. I entered the house, and my uncle said to me: 'You only wanted that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would call you a liar and hate you.'" He said: "Until Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed ﴿When the hypocrites come to you﴾." He said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent for me, recited it, and then said: 'Indeed Allah, mighty and majestic, has confirmed you, O Zayd.'"

• Abu Kurayb and al-Qasim ibn Bishr ibn Ma'ruf narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Bukayr narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, saying: al-Hakam said: "Inform me," he said: "I heard Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi say: I heard Zayd ibn Arqam say: When Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul said what he said, 'Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of Allah until they disperse,' and said, 'If we return to Medina,'" he said: "I heard it, so I went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and reported that. Some of the Ansar met him, and he came and swore that he had not said that. I returned to my home and slept." He said: "Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to me, or word reached me, so I went to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said: 'Indeed Allah, blessed and exalted, has confirmed you and excused you.'" He said: "Then the verse was revealed: ﴿They are the ones who say, 'Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of Allah'﴾ ... the verse."

• Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Hashim Abu al-Nadr narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from al-Hakam, who said: I heard Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi say: I heard Zayd ibn Arqam narrate this hadith.

• Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from al-Hakam, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, from Zayd ibn Arqam, who said: "We were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on a military expedition, and Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul said, ﴿If we return to Medina, the mightier will surely expel the meaner from it﴾." He said: "I went to the Prophet (ﷺ) and informed him, and Abd Allah ibn Ubayy swore that nothing of that had been said." He said: "My people blamed me and said: 'What did you want with this?' So I left and slept, distressed or grieved." He said: "Then the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) sent for me, or I came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said: 'Indeed Allah has revealed your excuse and confirmed you.'" He said: "And this verse was revealed: ﴿They are the ones who say, 'Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of Allah until they disperse'﴾ ... until ﴿If we return to Medina, the mightier will surely expel the meaner from it﴾."

• Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Adi narrated to us, saying: Ibn Awn informed me, from Muhammad, who said: "Zayd ibn Arqam heard it and reported it to his guardian. His guardian then reported it to the Prophet (ﷺ). It was said to Zayd: 'Your ear has been faithful.'"

• Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Ramadi narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn al-Hakam ibn Aban narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: Bishr ibn Muslim narrated to me: "It was said to Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul: 'O Abu Habbab, indeed severe verses have been revealed about you. Go to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) so that he may ask forgiveness for you.' He twisted his head and said: 'You ordered me to believe, and I believed. You ordered me to give the zakat (obligatory alms) on my wealth, and I gave it. Nothing remains but that I prostrate to Muhammad.'"

• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: "﴿And when it is said to them, 'Come, the Messenger of Allah will ask forgiveness for you,' they twist their heads﴾ ... the whole verse, which he recited up to ﴿the defiant ones﴾. It was revealed concerning Abd Allah ibn Ubayy, because a youth from among his relatives went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and told him a statement attributed to him, of a severe matter. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) summoned him, and he swore and disavowed that. The Ansar turned to that youth and blamed and reproached him. It was said to Abd Allah: 'If only you would go to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).' He began twisting his head, meaning: I will not do it, and he was lying about me. So Allah revealed what you hear."

• Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿And when it is said to them, "Come, the Messenger of Allah will ask forgiveness for you," they twist their heads﴾. He said: "It is Abd Allah ibn Ubayy. He was told: 'Come, so that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) may ask forgiveness for you.' He twisted his head and said: 'What did you say?'"

• Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, who said: "His people said to him: 'If only you would go to the Prophet (ﷺ) so that he may ask forgiveness for you.' He began twisting his head, so this was revealed about him: ﴿And when it is said to them, 'Come, the Messenger of Allah will ask forgiveness for you'﴾."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 63, verses 6–7:

The explanation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿It is the same for them whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them; Allah will never forgive them. Indeed, Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people.﴾ (6)

He, the Exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: It is the same for them, O Muhammad, these hypocrites to whom it was said, "Come, the Messenger of Allah will ask forgiveness for you," ﴿whether you ask forgiveness for them﴾ for their sins ﴿or do not ask forgiveness for them, Allah will never forgive them.﴾ He means: Allah will not pardon them for their sins, but will punish them for them. ﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people.﴾ He means: Indeed, Allah does not grant success in faith to the people who lie against Him, disbelieve in Him, and go out from His obedience.

It has been narrated to me by Muhammad ibn Sa'd, who said: my father related to me, who said: my paternal uncle related to me, who said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿It is the same for them whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them; Allah will never forgive them.﴾ He said: This verse was revealed after the verse in Surat at-Tawbah: ﴿Even if you ask forgiveness for them seventy times, Allah will not forgive them﴾ [at-Tawbah: 80]. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I will ask more than seventy times," so Allah revealed: ﴿It is the same for them whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them; Allah will never forgive them.﴾

* *

The explanation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿They are the ones who say, "Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of Allah until they disperse." And to Allah belong the treasures of the heavens and the earth, but the hypocrites do not understand.﴾ (7)

He, the Exalted, says: ﴿They are the ones who say﴾, meaning the hypocrites who say to their companions, ﴿"Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of Allah"﴾ from among his companions, the emigrants, ﴿until they disperse﴾. He means: until they scatter away from him.

And His saying: ﴿And to Allah belong the treasures of the heavens and the earth﴾

He means: To Allah belongs everything that is in the heavens and the earth, and in His hand are the keys to the treasures of all of it. No one can give anything to anyone except by His will. ﴿But the hypocrites do not understand﴾ that this is so; therefore they say: "Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ until they disperse."

The people of interpretation have said what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said this:

It has been narrated to me by Muhammad ibn Sa'd, who said: my father related to me, who said: my paternal uncle related to me, who said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿They are the ones who say, "Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of Allah until they disperse."﴾ He said: Do not feed Muhammad and his companions until hunger afflicts them, so they abandon their Prophet.

Bishr narrated to us, who said: Yazid related to us, who said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿They are the ones who say, "Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of Allah until they disperse."﴾ He recited it up to the end of the verse, and this is the statement of 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy to his hypocrite companions: "Do not spend on Muhammad and his companions until they abandon him, for if you did not spend on them, they would leave him and scatter away from him."

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, who said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿They are the ones who say, "Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of Allah until they disperse."﴾ 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul said to his companions: "Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of Allah, for if you do not spend on them, they will disperse."

It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd related to us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: ﴿Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of Allah until they disperse﴾: it means the support and assistance, and it does not mean the obligatory zakat; and those who said this were the hypocrites.

Al-Rabi' ibn Sulayman narrated to us, who said: Asad ibn Musa related to us, who said: Yahya ibn Abi Za'idah related to us, who said: al-A'mash related to us, from 'Amr ibn Murrah, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from Zayd ibn Arqam, who said: "When Ibn Ubayy said what he said, I informed the Prophet ﷺ, and he came and swore an oath. The people began saying to me: 'You bring the Messenger of Allah ﷺ a lie?' until I sat in the house, fearing that if they saw me they would say: 'This is the one who lies,' until ﴿They are the ones who say﴾ was revealed."

It has been narrated to me by Muhammad ibn Sa'd, who said: my father related to me, who said: my paternal uncle related to me, who said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿They are the ones who say, "Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of Allah until they disperse."﴾ He said: Do not feed Muhammad and his companions until hunger afflicts them, so they abandon their Prophet.

Bishr narrated to us, who said: Yazid related to us, who said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿They are the ones who say, "Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of Allah until they disperse."﴾ He recited it up to the end of the verse, and this is the statement of 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy to his hypocrite companions: "Do not spend on Muhammad and his companions until they abandon him, for if you did not spend on them, they would leave him and scatter away from him."

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, who said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿They are the ones who say, "Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of Allah until they disperse."﴾ 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul said to his companions: "Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of Allah, for if you do not spend on them, they will disperse."

It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd related to us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: ﴿Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of Allah until they disperse﴾: it means the support and assistance, and it does not mean the obligatory zakat; and those who said this were the hypocrites.

Al-Rabi' ibn Sulayman narrated to us, who said: Asad ibn Musa related to us, who said: Yahya ibn Abi Za'idah related to us, who said: al-A'mash related to us, from 'Amr ibn Murrah, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from Zayd ibn Arqam, who said: "When Ibn Ubayy said what he said, I informed the Prophet ﷺ, and he came and swore an oath. The people began saying to me: 'You bring the Messenger of Allah ﷺ a lie?' until I sat in the house, fearing that if they saw me they would say: 'This is the one who lies,' until ﴿They are the ones who say﴾ was revealed."

The exposition of His words, may He be exalted: ﴿They say, "If we return to Medina, the more honourable will surely expel the more humble from it." But to God belongs honour, and to His Messenger and to the believers; but the hypocrites do not know﴾ (63:8).

Says God, may His remembrance be exalted: These hypocrites, whose characteristics were described earlier, say ﴿If we return to Medina, the more honourable will surely expel the more humble from it﴾ (i.e., from it). By "the more honourable" (al-a'azz) he means the more forceful and the stronger. God, may His praise be exalted, said ﴿But to God belongs honour﴾, meaning might and strength, ﴿and to His Messenger and to the believers﴾ in God, ﴿but the hypocrites do not know﴾ that.

It has been mentioned that the cause of this saying was that 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy said it because a man from the Muhajirun had kicked a man from the Ansar.

Those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Ma'mar narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Amir narrated to us, saying: Zam'ah narrated to us, from 'Amr, who said: I heard Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah say: The Ansar were more numerous than the Muhajirun. Then the Muhajirun became numerous, and they went out on a military expedition (ghazwa). A man from the Muhajirun kicked a man from the Ansar. There was fighting between them until the one called out, "O people of the Ansar!" and the Muhajir called out, "O people of the Muhajirun!" The news reached the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said, "What is with you and the call of the Jahiliyya?" They said, "A man from the Muhajirun kicked a man from the Ansar." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said, "Leave it, for it is foul." 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul said, "If we return to Medina, the more honourable will surely expel the more humble from it." 'Umar said, "O Messenger of God, let me strike his neck." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said, "People must not say that the Messenger of God kills his companions."

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿They say, "If we return to Medina"﴾ ... to ﴿But to God belongs honour, and to His Messenger﴾, he said: 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul al-Ansari, the head of the hypocrites, said that, along with some hypocrites with him.

Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Ramadi narrated to me, saying: Ibrahim ibn al-Hakam narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to me, from 'Ikrimah, that 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul was called Hubab. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) named him 'Abd Allah. He said, "O Messenger of God, my father harms God and His Messenger, so leave me to kill him." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said to him, "Do not kill your father, 'Abd Allah." Then he came again and said, "O Messenger of God, my father harms God and His Messenger, so leave me to kill him." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said to him, "Do not kill your father." He said, "O Messenger of God, then perform ablution so that I may give him to drink from your ablution water; perhaps his heart will soften." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) performed ablution and gave it to him. He went with it to his father and gave him to drink. Then he said to him, "Do you know what I have given you to drink?" His father said, "Yes, you have given me the urine of your mother." His son said, "No, by God, but I have given you the ablution water of the Messenger of God (ﷺ)." 'Ikrimah said: 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy was of great standing among them. And concerning them this verse was revealed about the hypocrites: ﴿They are the ones who say, "Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of God until they disperse"﴾, and he is the one who said ﴿If we return to Medina, the more honourable will surely expel the more humble from it﴾. He said: When they reached Medina, the city of the Messenger (ﷺ) and of those with him, his son drew the sword and said to his father, "You claim, 'If we return to Medina, the more honourable will surely expel the more humble from it.' By God, you will not enter it until the Messenger of God (ﷺ) gives you permission."

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, that a man from the Muhajirun kicked a man from the Ansar with his foot, and that was during a severe (affair) concerning the people of Yemen. He called out, "O Muhajirun!" and the Ansar called out, "O Ansar!" He said: The Muhajirun were then more numerous than the Ansar. The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Leave it, for it is foul." 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul said, "If we return to Medina, the more honourable will surely expel the more humble from it."

Imran ibn Bakkar al-Kala'i narrated to me, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: 'Ali ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: Abu Ishaq narrated to us, that Zayd ibn Arqam informed him that 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul said, ﴿Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of God until they disperse﴾, and said, ﴿If we return to Medina, the more honourable will surely expel the more humble from it﴾. He said: Zayd informed me that he told the Messenger of God (ﷺ) what 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy had said. He said: Then 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy came and swore to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) that he had not said that. Abu Ishaq said: Zayd said to me: I sat in my house until God revealed the confirmation of Zayd and the refutation of 'Abd Allah in ﴿When the hypocrites come to you﴾.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿If we return to Medina, the more honourable will surely expel the more humble from it﴾, he recited the whole verse up to ﴿but they do not know﴾ and said: It was said by a hypocrite of great hypocrisy concerning two men who fought, one of them from Ghifar and the other from Juhayna. The Ghifari prevailed over the Juhani. Between Juhayna and the Ansar there was an alliance. A man from the hypocrites, who was Ibn Ubayy, said, "O sons of al-Aws, O sons of al-Khazraj, your companion and your ally has been overpowered!" Then he said, "By God, our situation and that of Muhammad is only like what the sayer said: 'Fatten your dog and it will devour you.' By God, if we return to Medina, the more honourable will surely expel the more humble from it." Some of them reported it to the Prophet of God (ﷺ). 'Umar said, "O Prophet of God, order Mu'adh ibn Jabal to strike the neck of this hypocrite." He said, "People must not speak of it that Muhammad kills his companions."

It was mentioned to us that a man among the hypocrites was often spoken to in his presence, and he was asked, "Does he pray?" He said, "Yes, but there is no good in his prayer." Then (the Prophet) said, "I have been forbidden from (the company of) those who pray; I have been forbidden from (the company of) those who pray."

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, who said: Two men fought, one of them from Juhayna and the other from Ghifar. Juhayna were allies of the Ansar. The Ghifari prevailed over him. A man among them, one of great hypocrisy, said, "Your companion! Your companion!" "By God, our situation and that of Muhammad is only like what the sayer said: 'Fatten your dog and it will devour you.' Indeed, by God, if we return to Medina, the more honourable will surely expel the more humble from it." They were on a journey. A man among those who heard it came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and informed him of that. 'Umar said, "Order Mu'adh to strike his neck." He said, "By God, people must not speak of it that Muhammad kills his companions." Then there was revealed concerning them: ﴿They are the ones who say, "Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of God"﴾ and His words ﴿If we return to Medina, the more honourable will surely expel the more humble from it﴾.

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Hasan, that a boy came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said, "O Messenger of God, I heard 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy say such and such." He said, "Perhaps you were angry with him?" He said, "No, by God, I heard him say it." He said, "Perhaps your hearing was mistaken?" He said, "No, by God, O Prophet of God, I heard him say it." He said, "Perhaps it was confused for you." He said, "No, by God." Then God revealed, as confirmation of the boy, ﴿If we return to Medina, the more honourable will surely expel the more humble from it﴾. The Prophet (ﷺ) took the boy's ear and said, "Your ear has been fulfilled, your ear has been fulfilled, O boy."

Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding God's words ﴿The more honourable will surely expel the more humble from it﴾: The hypocrites used to call the Muhajirun "the jallabib" (the coarse-robed ones). Ibn Ubayy said, "I have commanded you concerning these jallabib, my command." He said: This was between Amaj and 'Usfan at al-Kadid, when they disputed over the water, and the Muhajirun had prevailed over the water. He said: Ibn Ubayy also said, "By God, if we return to Medina, the more honourable will surely expel the more humble from it. I told you, 'Do not spend on them; if you leave them, they will not find anything to eat, and they will go out and flee.'" 'Umar ibn al-Khattab came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said, "O Messenger of God, do you not hear what Ibn Ubayy says?" He said, "And what is that?" He informed him and said, "Let me strike his neck, O Messenger of God." He said, "If you do, noses will tremble for him in Yathrib." 'Umar said, "If you dislike that a man of the Muhajirun should kill him, then let Sa'd ibn Mu'adh and Muhammad ibn Maslamah pass by him and they will kill him." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said, "I dislike that people should say that Muhammad kills his companions. Call 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy to me." He was called, and he said, "Do you not see what your father says?" He said, "And what does my father say, may I be your ransom?" He said, "He says, 'If we return to Medina, the more honourable will surely expel the more humble from it.'" He said, "By God, O Messenger of God, he has spoken the truth. You are the more honourable and he is the more humble. By God, when I came to Medina, O Messenger of God, the people of Yathrib knew that no one there was more dutiful than I. And if it pleases God and His Messenger that I bring you his head, I will bring it to you." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said, "No." When they reached Medina, 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy stood at its gate with a sword for his father. Then he said, "You are the one who said, 'If we return to Medina, the more honourable will surely expel the more humble from it.' By God, you will know honour belongs to you or to the Messenger of God. By God, his shade will not shelter you, and you will not be sheltered by it ever, except with permission from God and His Messenger." He said, "O Khazraj, my son is preventing me from my home! O Khazraj, my son is preventing me from my home!" He said, "By God, you will not be sheltered by it ever, except with his permission." Men gathered to him and spoke with him, and he said, "By God, he will not enter it except with permission from God and His Messenger." They came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and informed him, and he said, "Go to him and say to him, 'Let him be and his dwelling.'" They came to him and he said, "As for when the command of the Prophet (ﷺ) has come, then very well."

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah and 'Ali ibn Mujahid narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from 'Asim ibn 'Umar ibn Qatadah, from 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr, and from Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Hibban, who said: Each of them narrated to me part of the account of the Banu al-Mustaliq. They said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) received word that the Banu al-Mustaliq were gathering against him, and their leader was al-Harith ibn Abi Dirar, the father of Juwayriyya bint al-Harith, wife of the Prophet (ﷺ). When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) heard of them, he set out toward them until he met them at a water of theirs called al-Muraysi', on the side of Qudayd toward the coast. The people engaged, and they fought, and God defeated the Banu al-Mustaliq; those among them who were killed were killed, and the Messenger of God (ﷺ) took as spoils their children, women and property, which God gave to him as booty (fay'). A man of the Banu Kalb ibn 'Awf ibn 'Amir ibn Layth ibn Bakr, called Hisham ibn Subabah, was struck by a man of the Ansar from the family of 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit, who thought he was from the enemy, and so he killed him by mistake. While the people were at that water, the watering-crowd came, and with 'Umar ibn al-Khattab was a hired man of his from the Banu Ghifar called Jahjaha ibn Sa'id [[in the Sira of Ibn Hisham: Ibn Mas'ud]], who was leading his horse. Jahjaha and Sinan al-Juhani, ally of the Banu 'Awf ibn al-Khazraj, jostled over the water and fought. The Juhani cried, "O people of the Ansar!" and Jahjaha cried, "O people of the Muhajirun!" 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul became angry, and with him was a group of his people, among them Zayd ibn Arqam, a young boy of recent age. He said, "Have they done this? They have contended with us and outnumbered us in our lands. By God, we and these coarse-robed ones of Quraysh are only like what the sayer said: 'Fatten your dog and it will devour you.' By God, if we return to Medina, the more honourable will surely expel the more humble from it." Then he turned to those of his people present and said, "This is what you have done to yourselves: you have let them into your lands and shared your wealth with them. By God, if you withheld what is in your hands from them, they would move away from your lands to elsewhere." Zayd ibn Arqam heard that and walked with it to the Messenger of God (ﷺ), at the end of his military expedition. He reported the news, and 'Umar ibn al-Khattab was with him, and he said, "O Messenger of God, order 'Abbad ibn Bishr ibn Waqsh to kill him." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said, "Then how, O 'Umar, when people speak of it that Muhammad kills his companions? No, but proclaim the departure." That was at an hour in which the Messenger of God (ﷺ) did not usually depart, so the people set out. 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy had gone to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) when it reached him that Zayd ibn Arqam had conveyed what he had said, and he swore by God that he had not said what was said and had not spoken it. 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy was a great nobleman among his people. Those Ansar among the Prophet's companions who were present said, "O Messenger of God, perhaps the boy has erred in his account and did not remember what the man said," out of compassion for 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy and to defend him. When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) had set out and proceeded, Usayd ibn Hudayr met him, greeted him with the greeting of prophethood, and said, "O Messenger of God, you have set out at an unpleasant hour, at which you did not usually set out." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said, "Has it not reached you what your companion said?" He said, "Which companion, O Messenger of God?" He said, "'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy." He said, "And what did he say?" He said, "He claims that if he returns to Medina, he will expel the more honourable from it, the more humble." Usayd said, "By God, you, O Messenger of God, will expel him if you wish. By God, he is the humble one and you are the honourable one. Then, O Messenger of God, be gentle with him, for by God, God brought you when his people were stringing beads to crown him, for he sees that you have taken a kingdom from him." Then the Messenger of God (ﷺ) went on with the people that day until evening, and that night until morning, and returned with them that day until the sun troubled them. Then he halted with the people, and they had hardly touched the ground before they fell asleep. He did that only to occupy the people away from the matter that had been the previous day's talk about 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy. Then he set off with the people and took the way of the Hijaz until he halted at a water in the Hijaz beyond al-Naqi', called Naq'a. When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) set off, a strong wind blew over the people, troubling them, and they feared it. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said, "Do not fear, for it has blown only for the death of a great one among the great unbelievers." When they reached Medina, they found that Rifa'ah ibn Zayd ibn al-Tabut, of the Banu Qaynuqa', who was one of the great Jews and a refuge for the hypocrites, had died that day. Then the surah in which God mentioned the hypocrites was revealed concerning 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul and those who were with him in his manner, and He said ﴿When the hypocrites come to you﴾. When this surah was revealed, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) took Zayd's ear and said, "This is the one whose ear God has fulfilled." And news reached 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy of what had happened with his father.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to me, from 'Asim ibn 'Umar ibn Qatadah, that 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said, "O Messenger of God, it has reached me that you intend to kill 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy, because of what has reached you about him. If you are going to do it, then order me, and I will bring you his head. By God, the Khazraj know that there was no man more dutiful to his father than I. I fear that you will order someone else to kill him, and then my soul will not let me look at the killer of 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy walking among the people while I do nothing, so I would kill a believer for an unbeliever and enter the Fire." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said, "Rather, we will be gentle with him and keep good company with him as long as he remains with us." After that day, whenever an incident occurred, it was his people who would reproach him, seize him, rebuke him and threaten him. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said to 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, when this news of their conduct reached him, "How do you see it, O 'Umar? By God, if I had killed him on the day you ordered me to kill him, noses would have trembled for him. If you ordered them today to kill him, they would kill him." 'Umar said, "By God, I know that the command of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) is far greater in blessing than my command."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 63, verse 9:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, let not your wealth or your children divert you from the remembrance of Allah. And whoever does that—then those are the losers.﴾

He, exalted is His mention, says: O you who have affirmed Allah and His Messenger, ﴿let not your wealth divert you﴾, meaning: let not your wealth make you necessary (lawajib) for you, ﴿nor your children﴾, [diversion (al-lahw)] ﴿from the remembrance of Allah﴾. It is from "alhaytuhu 'an kadhā wa kadhā" (I diverted him from such and such), so he is diverted (yalhu lahwan). From it is the saying of Imru' al-Qays:

"And [with] a woman like you, pregnant and nursing, I diverted her from the one with amulets, the weaned infant."[[The verse is by Imru' al-Qays. The author's citation of it was previously mentioned in volume 17 (17: 114), and we explained it there in detail, so refer back to it. The point of evidence here is his saying "fa-alhaytuhā" (so I diverted her). Its root is from al-lahw, which is what you are diverted and amused by and what occupies you, from desire, delight and the like. It is said: lahawtu bi-l-shay' alhū bihi lahwan (I was diverted by the thing), and talahaytu bihi when you amuse yourself, occupy yourself with it, and become heedless of other things by it. And you say: alhānī fulān ʿan kadhā, meaning he occupied me and made me forget, and the hamzah in it appears to indicate removal (al-salb).]] It was said: by the remembrance of Allah, exalted is His praise, in this place is meant the five daily prayers.

Mention of those who said that:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Mihran narrated to us, from Abu Sinan, from Thabit, from al-Dahhak, regarding ﴿O you who have believed, let not your wealth or your children divert you from the remembrance of Allah﴾, he said: the five daily prayers.

And His saying: ﴿And whoever does that﴾

meaning: and whoever is diverted by his wealth and children from the remembrance of Allah, ﴿then those are the losers﴾, meaning: they are the ones who are cheated of their portion of the honor and mercy of Allah, blessed and exalted is He.

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And spend of that which We have provided for you, before death comes to one of you and he says, "My Lord, if only You would delay me for a near term, so I would give charity and be among the righteous."﴾ (10) ﴿But Allah will never delay a soul when its time has come; and Allah is Acquainted with what you do.﴾ (11)

He, dhikruhu (exalted is His mention), says: Spend, O believers in Allah and His Messenger, from the wealth that We have provided you, before death comes to one of you and he says when death descends upon him: "My Lord, why did You not delay me for a near term, so that I might be given respite in my term until a near time, so I would give charity" – meaning: so I would purify my wealth – ﴿and be among the righteous﴾ – meaning: and act in obedience to You, and fulfil Your obligations.

It was also said: by His saying ﴿and be among the righteous﴾ is meant: and perform Hajj to Your Sacred House.

And in accordance with what we have said regarding this, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have spoken.

Those who said that:

Yunus and Sa'id ibn al-Rabi' narrated to me, Sa'id saying: Sufyan narrated to us, and Yunus saying: Sufyan informed us, from Abu Janab, from al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "No one dies without having paid the zakat of his wealth or performed Hajj except that he asks for a return (al-karrah). They said: O Abu 'Abbas, you keep bringing us things we do not recognize. He said: I will recite to you from the Book of Allah: ﴿And spend of that which We have provided for you, before death comes to one of you and he says, 'My Lord, if only You would delay me for a near term, so I would give charity'﴾ – he said: I will pay the zakat of my wealth – ﴿and be among the righteous﴾ – he said: I will perform Hajj."

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Sinan, from a man, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "What prevents one of you, if he has wealth on which zakat is obligatory, from paying zakat, and if he is able to perform Hajj, from performing it before death comes to him, so that he asks his Lord for a return and is not given it?" A man said: "Do you not fear Allah? The believer asks for a return?" He said: "Yes. I will recite to you a Qur'an," and he recited ﴿O you who believe, let not your wealth or your children divert you from the remembrance of Allah﴾. The man said: "What, then, makes Hajj obligatory upon me?" He said: "A mount to carry you and provision to convey you."

Abbad ibn Ya'qub al-Asadi and Fudalah ibn al-Fadl narrated to us; Abbad said: Yazid Abu Hazim, the freedman of al-Dahhak, informed us.

Fudalah said: Bazi' narrated to us from al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim concerning His saying ﴿if only You would delay me for a near term, so I would give charity﴾: "I would give charity from the zakat of my wealth" – ﴿and be among the righteous﴾ – "the Hajj."

I was told on the authority of al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd narrated to us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say concerning His saying ﴿Let not your wealth or your children divert you from the remembrance of Allah﴾ to the end of the surah: "It is the believing man in whom death has come, who has much wealth which he has not paid zakat on, nor performed Hajj with, nor given the right of Allah from it. He asks for a return at death, so that he may pay zakat from his wealth. Allah says: (But Allah will never delay a soul when its time has come)."

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿Let not your wealth or your children divert you from the remembrance of Allah﴾ ... to His saying ﴿And spend of that which We have provided for you, before death comes to one of you﴾: "It is the believing man when death descends upon him, and he has wealth which he has not paid zakat on, nor performed Hajj with, nor given the right of Allah in it, so he asks for a return at death in order to give charity from his wealth and pay zakat." Allah says ﴿But Allah will never delay a soul when its time has come﴾.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan: ﴿so I would give charity and be among the righteous﴾ – "Zakat and Hajj."

The readers differed concerning the recitation of His saying ﴿and be among the righteous﴾. The majority of the readers of the regional cities recited it as "wa-akun" (وَأَكُنْ) in the jussive, as a conjunction with His saying ﴿fa-assaddaqa﴾ as though the fa were not there, since ﴿fa-assaddaqa﴾, if the fa were not in it, would be jussive. But Ibn Muhaysin and Abu 'Amr recited it as "wa-akun" (وَأَكُونَ) with the wa retained and in the accusative, as a conjunction with His saying ﴿fa-assaddaqa﴾, so that ﴿wa-akun﴾ is accusative because ﴿fa-assaddaqa﴾ is accusative.

The correct view on this is that both are well-known recitations, and whichever of them the reciter reads is correct.

And His saying ﴿But Allah will never delay a soul when its time has come﴾.

He says: Allah will never delay the term of anyone, extending it for him when his term arrives, but He will take him. ﴿And Allah is Acquainted with what you do﴾ – He says: And Allah is possessed of awareness and knowledge of the deeds of His servants; He encompasses all of them, nothing is hidden from Him, and He will recompense them for them, rewarding the doer of good for his good, and the doer of evil for his evil.

End of the interpretation of Surah al-Munafiqun.

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And spend of that which We have provided for you, before death comes to one of you and he says, "My Lord, if only You would delay me for a near term, so I would give charity and be among the righteous."﴾ (10) ﴿But Allah will never delay a soul when its time has come; and Allah is Acquainted with what you do.﴾ (11)

He, dhikruhu (exalted is His mention), says: Spend, O believers in Allah and His Messenger, from the wealth that We have provided you, before death comes to one of you and he says when death descends upon him: "My Lord, why did You not delay me for a near term, so that I might be given respite in my term until a near time, so I would give charity" – meaning: so I would purify my wealth – ﴿and be among the righteous﴾ – meaning: and act in obedience to You, and fulfil Your obligations.

It was also said: by His saying ﴿and be among the righteous﴾ is meant: and perform Hajj to Your Sacred House.

And in accordance with what we have said regarding this, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have spoken.

Those who said that:

Yunus and Sa'id ibn al-Rabi' narrated to me, Sa'id saying: Sufyan narrated to us, and Yunus saying: Sufyan informed us, from Abu Janab, from al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "No one dies without having paid the zakat of his wealth or performed Hajj except that he asks for a return (al-karrah). They said: O Abu 'Abbas, you keep bringing us things we do not recognize. He said: I will recite to you from the Book of Allah: ﴿And spend of that which We have provided for you, before death comes to one of you and he says, 'My Lord, if only You would delay me for a near term, so I would give charity'﴾ – he said: I will pay the zakat of my wealth – ﴿and be among the righteous﴾ – he said: I will perform Hajj."

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Sinan, from a man, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "What prevents one of you, if he has wealth on which zakat is obligatory, from paying zakat, and if he is able to perform Hajj, from performing it before death comes to him, so that he asks his Lord for a return and is not given it?" A man said: "Do you not fear Allah? The believer asks for a return?" He said: "Yes. I will recite to you a Qur'an," and he recited ﴿O you who believe, let not your wealth or your children divert you from the remembrance of Allah﴾. The man said: "What, then, makes Hajj obligatory upon me?" He said: "A mount to carry you and provision to convey you."

Abbad ibn Ya'qub al-Asadi and Fudalah ibn al-Fadl narrated to us; Abbad said: Yazid Abu Hazim, the freedman of al-Dahhak, informed us.

Fudalah said: Bazi' narrated to us from al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim concerning His saying ﴿if only You would delay me for a near term, so I would give charity﴾: "I would give charity from the zakat of my wealth" – ﴿and be among the righteous﴾ – "the Hajj."

I was told on the authority of al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd narrated to us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say concerning His saying ﴿Let not your wealth or your children divert you from the remembrance of Allah﴾ to the end of the surah: "It is the believing man in whom death has come, who has much wealth which he has not paid zakat on, nor performed Hajj with, nor given the right of Allah from it. He asks for a return at death, so that he may pay zakat from his wealth. Allah says: (But Allah will never delay a soul when its time has come)."

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿Let not your wealth or your children divert you from the remembrance of Allah﴾ ... to His saying ﴿And spend of that which We have provided for you, before death comes to one of you﴾: "It is the believing man when death descends upon him, and he has wealth which he has not paid zakat on, nor performed Hajj with, nor given the right of Allah in it, so he asks for a return at death in order to give charity from his wealth and pay zakat." Allah says ﴿But Allah will never delay a soul when its time has come﴾.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan: ﴿so I would give charity and be among the righteous﴾ – "Zakat and Hajj."

But Ibn Muhaysin and Abu 'Amr recited it as "wa-akun" (وَأَكُونَ) with the wa retained and in the accusative, as a conjunction with His saying ﴿fa-assaddaqa﴾, so that ﴿wa-akun﴾ is accusative because ﴿fa-assaddaqa﴾ is accusative.

The correct view on this is that both are well-known recitations, and whichever of them the reciter reads is correct.
